submission.justification: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage achieves the highest light collection of 54.372 PE/MeV among all tested configurations. This represents approximately 40% better performance than Module-D3 (39.122 PE/MeV) and 121% better than Module-D2 (24.593 PE/MeV) at the same coverage. The 30% coverage is at the maximum allowed limit, which maximizes light collection as it scales approximately as coverage^0.8. While Module-D1's thin bonded dichroic filter design requires careful thermal cycling qualification to ensure the failure rate remains below 5% after 20 thermal cycles (300K to 87K), this is a standard validation requirement for all candidate modules. The electronics have been validated for all designs, and sufficient feedthrough capacity exists for 30% coverage. Given that the primary goal is to achieve the highest possible light collection and Module-D1 is listed as an official candidate design, this configuration provides the best physics performance for the far detector.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (PE/MeV)
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 at 30% coverage achieves 54.372 PE/MeV, which is the highest among all tested configurations including D1 at lower coverages (44.336 at 25%, 38.908 at 20%), D3 at all coverages (39.122 at 30%, 30.583 at 25%, 27.141 at 20%), and D2 (24.593 at 30%).

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 (large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter) is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate designs in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules may fail after 20 thermal cycles (300K to 87K)
requirements.evidence: No explicit thermal cycling failure rate data is provided in the project documents for any of the candidate modules. This qualification testing must be performed as part of standard module validation before the design freeze in Q3. The thin bonded interface in Module-D1 requires particular attention during thermal cycling qualification.
Recommended coverage of 30% is at the maximum allowed limit and is supported by available feedthrough capacity as confirmed in meeting notes from 2026-01-20.
